extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians attending or presenting at the American Mathematical Society (AMS) meeting (Iowa City, March 1996)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and descriptive labels governing contributed and special-session presentations at the AMS meeting: time limits, presenter designation, audience-interest flags, abstract indexing, and labeling of talk status (e.g., 'Preliminary report').

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for contributed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for each contributed paper in the sessions is ten minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Special Sessions the time limit varies from session to session and within sessions. To maintain the schedule, time limits will be strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenter indication for multi-author papers (asterisk)
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers with more than one author, an asterisk follows the name of the author who plans to present the paper at the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The asterisk is used in the program listing to identify which coauthor will give the talk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate-interest flag (solid triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers flagged with a solid triangle (.,..) have been designated by the author as being of possible interest to undergraduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may mark their abstracts to indicate potential undergraduate-level interest; the program displays this marker next to such papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts location and ordering scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts of papers presented in the sessions at this meeting will be found in the Spring 1996 issue of Abstracts of papers presented to the American Mathematical Society, ordered according to the numbers in parentheses following the listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The numbering encodes subject classification and receipt order: the middle two digits (e.g., in 897-20-1136) refer to the Mathematical Reviews subject classification assigned by the individual author; groups of papers for each subject are listed chronologically in the Abstracts. The last one to four digits (e.g., 897-20-1136) refer to the receipt number of the abstract; abstracts are further sorted by the receipt number within each classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Preliminary report' label denotes preliminary results/status
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Preliminary report' appended to a talk title indicates the talk reports preliminary results or work-in-progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many listings include the phrase 'Preliminary report' to signal the provisional nature of the material; attendees should interpret such talks as not presenting fully finalized results.
